title: Differences in Camera3D between editor and running game
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA RTX 500 Ada Generation Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H (22 threads) - 31.50 GiB memory

### Issue description

The projection matrix of a `Camera3D` and the result of calling `unproject_position()` are different for the same camera when in editor vs. when running the game.

The following code shows this behavior:
```gdscript
@tool
extends Node

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if (Engine.is_editor_hint()):
		print("Projection Matrix in editor:")	
	else:
		print("Projection Matrix in running game:")	
	print(%Camera3D.get_camera_projection())
	print()
	
	if (Engine.is_editor_hint()):
		print("Unproject in editor:")	
	else:
		print("Unproject in running game:")	
	print(%Camera3D.unproject_position(Vector3(0,0,0)))
	print()
```

While in editor, this prints:
```
Projection Matrix in editor:
[X: (1.303225, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0), Y: (0.0, 1.303225, 0.0, 0.0), Z: (0.0, 0.0, -1.000025, -1.0), W: (0.0, 0.0, -0.100001, 0.0)]

Unproject in editor:
(1.0, 1.0)
```

While running game, this prints:
```
Projection Matrix in running game:
[X: (0.733064, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0), Y: (0.0, 1.303225, 0.0, 0.0), Z: (0.0, 0.0, -1.000025, -1.0), W: (0.0, 0.0, -0.100001, 0.0)]

Unproject in running game:
(576.0, 324.0)
```

Note the difference in the first number of the projection matrix (all other values are equal), and the completely different unproject_position result. I assume the in-running-game results are correct and the editor results are wrong. 

This happens on a completely new project, with no changes to any project settings. Just a Camera3D in an otherwise empty scene.

I would expect this to return the same results by default. Or - at the least - offer some way of influencing how a camera behaves while in the editor. I understand that the target resolution is a part of the equation, but then what is the resolution that the camera uses while in editor? It seems like its square (hence the equal values in the projection matrix) and super low resolution.

Haven't found this exact issue in the tracker, but some that seem related and might hint at the same underlying problem:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106793
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75973#issuecomment-2524175396

### Steps to reproduce

Create a new project, add a `Camera3D ` to a `Node3D` scene and add the above code to a root script.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[camera-projection-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24392773/camera-projection-test.zip)
